name: Singapore American School
summary: Large US-curriculum Woodlands campus — geography is part of admissions, and learning-support capacity is competitive like peer inclusive schools.
body: SAS is one of Singapore’s largest international schools, offering an American pathway from early childhood through high school with AP options and extensive co-curriculars. The Woodlands campus is a full-day geographic commitment — families often live north/west or accept longer drives from central belts. Parent forums discussing SEN / neurodivergent support frequently shortlist SAS alongside Dover Court; community reports have cited multi-month to ~24-month waits for learning-support places in peak years — confirm current capacity in writing. Waitlists and admissions cycles are competitive for popular grades; start early if your move is package-timed, and ask HR about any corporate nomination pathways in writing. Peer threads that crown SAS as the only ‘gold standard’ American option still need a dated seat email — short-notice relocations often land a bridge school first. Tour with commute maths and learning-support questions in hand, not just the theatre and pool. PTC and student-led conference formats change by division — dual-career households should book early and send a one-page brief if only one adult can attend. Ask how learning-support waitlists and mid-year entry handoffs are communicated to dual-career parents — calendar-ready review windows beat vague “we will be in touch.” Dual-career note: book-week parade call times and costume blackouts need a named hall adult on the shared calendar before client week.
waitlistNotes: Plan 6–12+ months ahead for peak grades and learning-support places; sibling priority and corporate nomination policies vary — verify in writing. Community reports of multi-month SEN waits should be confirmed with current admissions.
